meaning: to ease the symptoms of an illness or a wrong without removing its cause
sentence: Morphine could palliate the pain, but nothing could touch the disease itself.

meaning: a remedy or measure that relieves symptoms without curing the cause; also, relieving rather than curing
sentence: The allowance was a palliative; the grievance behind the strike was left untouched.

meaning: belonging to the open sea, away from the coast and the sea floor
sentence: Tuna are pelagic fish that spend their whole lives far from any shore.

meaning: so clear that one can see straight through it, said of water or of writing
sentence: The stream ran so pellucid that every pebble on the bed stood out.

meaning: extreme poverty, the state of having almost nothing
sentence: Years of illness and litigation reduced the family to penury.

meaning: something registered directly by the senses, as distinct from an idea formed about it
sentence: A flash of red is a percept; danger is the meaning the mind then builds on it.

meaning: an extra benefit or privilege attached to a post, over and above the pay
sentence: A staff car and free quarters were the perquisites of the appointment.

meaning: to harass or oppress somebody persistently, especially for their beliefs, race or politics
sentence: The sect fled the province when the governor began to persecute its followers.

meaning: the point of view from which something is regarded, and the sense of proportion that comes with it; also the art of showing depth on a flat surface
sentence: Seen from the villagers' perspective, the new road was a threat and not a gift.

meaning: having a keen mind that sees quickly into people and situations
sentence: A perspicacious young officer spotted the flaw in the plan before anyone else did.

meaning: clearness of expression, the quality of being easy to understand
sentence: The perspicuity of his orders left no room for anyone to misunderstand them.

meaning: clearly expressed and easily followed, said of writing or speech rather than of a mind
sentence: His perspicuous summary made a tangled case plain to the whole class.

meaning: stubbornly persistent in holding to an opinion or a purpose
sentence: Her pertinacious questioning finally shook the truth out of the witness.

meaning: relating to a planet or the planets; also, on a scale that covers the whole earth
sentence: Warming of this kind is a planetary problem and no single country can settle it.

meaning: easily bent without breaking; also easily influenced or talked round
sentence: Cane is pliable enough to be woven into the back of a chair.

meaning: bending or giving way readily, whether in substance or in temperament
sentence: The willow's pliant branches bowed right over in the gale and sprang back.

meaning: thickly inhabited, having a large number of people living in it
sentence: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in the country.

meaning: to come or go before something else in time, order or rank
sentence: A short briefing will precede the march at first light.

meaning: coming immediately before in time or order
sentence: The rule is set out in full in the preceding paragraph.

meaning: a rule or maxim laying down how one ought to behave
sentence: He lived by the old precept that a soldier's word is his bond.

meaning: a strong and settled liking for one thing over others
sentence: He had a predilection for old maps and second-hand bookshops.

meaning: attractive in appearance and creating a favourable first impression
sentence: He was not a prepossessing man, but he spoke with quiet authority.

meaning: something that must be in place beforehand as a condition of something else
sentence: A pass in mathematics is a prerequisite for the engineering course.

meaning: complete honesty and uprightness of character
sentence: His probity in handling the regiment's funds was never once in question.

meaning: showing disrespect for what is sacred; also, to treat a holy thing with irreverence
sentence: The men were warned not to profane the shrine by walking in with their boots on.

meaning: producing a great deal, whether of fruit, offspring or written work
sentence: A prolific writer, he brought out forty novels in thirty years.

meaning: dull and ordinary, with nothing imaginative or poetic about it
sentence: The truth behind the legend turned out to be dismayingly prosaic.

meaning: to forbid something by law or authority, or to outlaw a person
sentence: The new regulations proscribe the carrying of mobile phones into the hall.

meaning: to bring a criminal charge against somebody in a court of law; also, to carry something on to its finish
sentence: The state decided to prosecute the contractor for fraud.

meaning: to try to convert somebody to one's own religion or set of beliefs
sentence: He had come to the valley to teach, he insisted, not to proselytize.

meaning: expected or likely in the time to come, looking forward rather than back
sentence: Prospective candidates must register before the end of the month.

meaning: to draw something out so that it lasts longer than it need
sentence: Both sides seemed content to protract the talks indefinitely.

meaning: lasting far longer than was expected or than is usual
sentence: A protracted illness kept him out of the final selection.

meaning: relating to powers of the mind that ordinary science cannot explain; also, a person claiming such powers
sentence: She claimed a psychic warning of the accident a full hour before it happened.

meaning: inflicting punishment, or meant as a punishment
sentence: The court added punitive damages to the compensation already awarded.

meaning: lacking courage, timid and faint-hearted
sentence: It was a pusillanimous retreat from a promise he had made in public.
